title: Removing the defender

D0.outcome: Explains that a piece defended by one other piece can be won by taking, blocking, pinning or deflecting its only defender first.

D1.outcome: When told 'remove the defender', finds the capture or attack that eliminates the sole defender and wins the target.

D2.outcome: In mixed sets, finds the removal that wins material, and does not play it when the defender's job passes to another piece or the removal costs more than it wins.

D3.outcome: Recounts the square after the removal (recaptures, new defenders, check on recapture) and predicts how adding one defender changes the result.

misconceptions: Capturing the defender always wins the defended piece.
A defender can only be removed by capture.
sources: sources/sheets/edlasker_chess-strategy.md §4 K3 (the count lies: defender capturable by a cheaper piece, forced away, pinned); §7 row K3
sources/sheets/nimzowitsch_my-system.md §4 ideas 21, 27 (destroying a defender; exchange on the pinning square)
conditions: The defender's job is not taken over by another piece after it leaves.
After the removal, the count on the target square favours the attacker, including the recapture sequence.
A defender in the wide sense includes a piece guarding a file entry, an outpost or the castled king.
contrasts: Capturing with the very piece that is holding the king-side together removes your own best defender.
A second defender recaptures, so the removal gains nothing.
The 'defender' captured guards a square that has nothing of value on it.

soft_prereq_notes.TAC.DISCOVER.D2: a discovered attack can remove a defender with tempo
